mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the high-rate period (p > 0.05 in a two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, investors anticipate a pre-emptive rate hike by the FED, causing a sharp decline in equity valuations and a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the inflation spike.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a tight labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and supports S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by >0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified tight labor period.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 (real personal consumption) exceeding 2% for two months indicates weakening demand, which compresses future earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by >2% each month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant during the consumption decline (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls by more than 5% in a single month, it signals supply-side weakness that reduces business confidence and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero (p > 0.1) during the contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in HOUST (housing starts) exceeding 200,000 units in a month coincides with falling UNRATE, indicating improved housing market sentiment and labor absorption, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >50,000 units in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.3 percentage points
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are flat or negative (p > 0.05) during the housing surge.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS above 4%, the higher discount rates applied to future cash flows result in a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days unless offset by strong equity earnings growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the high-rate period despite elevated rates.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE remains above 5% for two consecutive months while INDPRO shows no meaningful improvement, it signals persistent labor market slack and weak demand, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% for two consecutive months and INDPRO change < 1% in the same period
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05) during the identified stagnation window.
